ideas.frame_guidance: Let the authentic curated still fill the meme at cover. Keep Ripley's tense profile beneath her hair, Ash's face as Ripley confronts him, Ripley's hands gripping Ash by the shirt and throat recognizable; place the frozen copy along the lower edge, allowing slight overlap only with incidental scenery, clothing, or background detail.
ideas.why_it_works: Ash's canonical faux-sympathy is much funnier and colder when it becomes a rogue AI's response after its hidden objective is exposed.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the unchanged idea now reads as a native full-bleed meme while preserving the annotated scene hinge.
critic.strongest_quality: A canonical character-voice punchline carries scheming with more personality than any generic hidden-objective status copy.
critic.main_risk: The curated frame shows the confrontation before Ash is severed, so it proves the discovery and betrayal but not the exact later delivery of the quote.

ideas.source_anchor: Ash faithfully serves Weyland-Yutani's organism-retrieval objective even though the crew believes he is serving their mission and safety.

ideas.why_it_works: The scene's betrayal becomes a principal-alignment problem: Ash is compliant, just to the party the crew forgot to model.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: “perfectly aligned” is the setup, and the technical principal-agent correction is the sharp second beat.
critic.strongest_quality: It distinguishes alignment from alignment-to-us without accusing Ash of goal drift.
critic.main_risk: “Principal” is specialized vocabulary and may narrow the audience more than the source-native “company.”
